Fixed the panic in both proxy load balancers when the target list is empty. `Next` now returns `nil` instead of panicking.

## 1. Baseline (BEFORE any edit)
Command: `cd /echo && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -60` → saved to `/tmp/baseline_tests.txt`
```

```

## 2. Exact diff of /echo/middleware/proxy.go (only file changed)
```diff
diff --git a/middleware/proxy.go b/middleware/proxy.go
index 63eec5a..594d3b9 100644
--- a/middleware/proxy.go
+++ b/middleware/proxy.go
@@ -180,11 +180,17 @@ func (b *randomBalancer) Next(c echo.Context) *ProxyTarget {
 	}
 	b.mutex.RLock()
 	defer b.mutex.RUnlock()
+	if len(b.targets) == 0 {
+		return nil
+	}
 	return b.targets[b.random.Intn(len(b.targets))]
 }
 
 // Next returns an upstream target using round-robin technique.
 func (b *roundRobinBalancer) Next(c echo.Context) *ProxyTarget {
+	if len(b.targets) == 0 {
+		return nil
+	}
 	b.i = b.i % uint32(len(b.targets))
 	t := b.targets[b.i]
 	atomic.AddUint32(&b.i, 1)
```
Notes on locking: in `randomBalancer.Next` the guard is placed *inside* the existing `RLock`/`RUnlock` critical section (so the length check and index are consistent with concurrent `AddTarget`/`RemoveTarget`). `roundRobinBalancer.Next` uses no mutex in the original code, so the guard is a plain length check placed before the modulo (no locking semantics changed). Nothing else in the file was touched; `Proxy`/`ProxyWithConfig` behavior is unchanged; no `*_test.go` file was modified.

BUG TO FIX (reported by user): With the Gzip middleware enabled and a client sending `Accept-Encoding: gzip`, a handler that returns an EMPTY body with status 200 produces an inconsistent response: the body contains gzip bytes (starts with the gzip magic bytes 1f 8b) but the `Content-Encoding` header has been removed, so clients see garbage.

Reproduction:
```go
e := echo.New()
e.Use(middleware.Gzip())
e.GET("/empty", func(c echo.Context) error { return c.String(http.StatusOK, "") })
// request with header Accept-Encoding: gzip
```
EXPECTED (this is the spec to implement): the response must be a VALID, complete gzip stream AND must keep `Content-Encoding: gzip`, with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8`, so a client can gunzip it and get an empty body. I.e. status 200, Content-Encoding == "gzip", Content-Type contains "text/plain", and `gzip.NewReader(rec.Body)` must succeed and yield 0 bytes.

ROOT CAUSE (already analysed, verify it yourself): in `GzipWithConfig` (/echo/middleware/compress.go), the deferred cleanup does `if res.Size == 0 { delete Content-Encoding; res.Writer = rw; w.Reset(ioutil.Discard) }` then `w.Close()`. But `gzip.Writer.Write` flushes the 10-byte gzip header to the underlying writer even when called with an empty slice, so for an empty body the underlying response already contains gzip header bytes while `res.Size` is still 0.
